These pads fixed all these problems. Over the two months we've had the pads installed, the washer has been much quieter for all loads and can easily handle large, hard-to-spin items (king size fleece blankets).

A word of advice on install: If your washer and dryer are tucked into a recessed nook or otherwise difficult to access from the side or behind, make sure you do the hardest to reach back corner first, then the other back corner, then the front ones. It becomes more difficult to lift the washer as you go.

We also bought a set for both washer and dryer so they'd match in height. Consider this if you are also OCD.

I have a 2 story townhome with a small laundry room. I had to be very thoughtful and careful in preparing for delivery of my new frontload washer and dryer. I wanted the biggest, but it just wouldn't fit. I also wanted pedestals, but was worried the drawer wouldn't slide out with the "per code" washer drain pan.

Since I was having these delivered and installed, I wanted to prepare for every possible thing that could go wrong. I bought a new low profile drain pan (ge, home depot) and bought 2 sets of these dampeners.

Sure enough, the drain pan needed to be swapped. Even then, the drawer still did not have the clearance. So I opened a pack of these to give to the installers. They had fits getting them in there in the tight space, but used windex to lubricate the floor so they could slide everything in to place (these things grip like crazy without lube). It worked perfectly. One thing though is that I had to cut a flat on 2 of the pucks so they would fit in the drain pan. Really easy with my miter saw.

I gave them the other pack to put under the dryer so they would match height wise, but they just rolled their eyes at me and left. Basically I tipped the dryer back and out 2 under the front. Then pulled back on the dryer and had my wife push the back 2 in place with a broom handle. Took all of 3 minutes to do this.

I used the pads to ease strong vibration of Bosch stacked washer/dryer that are installed on top/3rd (wooden, regular, unreinforced) floor in a house. Yes, it is in a dedicated washer/dryer room.

While the washer itself is very well balanced and has no vibration w/o anything inside (I tried empty run), it produces quite bad vibration with clothes no matter what kind of clothes we wash, to the point that the whole building structure resonates in the nearby room on high speed spin cycles. It was extremely annoying, not even saying dangerous to the building structure in the long term.

After reading a lot on the subject and having seen the recommendations to install such washers on concrete floors only (out of the question for me) I decided to try the pads, and the result was quite positive.

While the pads did not eliminate the issue completely, they did work really well; I would say at least 50% less vibration now, and the high speed spin cycles are more or less bearable now (not at all before). Slower spin cycles are completely unnoticeable right now as well (this was not the case before; even slower spins would cause the vibration one could hear/feel).

Definitely would recommend to try this option before investing in more complex fixes such as trying to reinforce the floors where washer/dryer are installed.
